labs.name: Physics Lab
labs.shortDescription: Build confidence with measurement and observation.

experiments.title: Measurement with a Vernier Caliper
experiments.objective: Measure a small object using a vernier caliper and record the instrument’s least count.
procedure: Identify the main scale and vernier scale, then check for zero error.
Place the object gently between the appropriate jaws.
Read the main scale and coinciding vernier division, applying any zero correction.
Repeat the measurement at several positions and record the readings with units.
experiments.expectedResult: Repeated readings agree within the instrument’s measurement resolution.
precautions: Do not force the jaws against the object.
Follow the reading method for the instrument provided by your instructor.

labs.name: Network Theory Lab
labs.shortDescription: Explore circuit equivalents and transient responses.

experiments.title: Verification of Thevenin's Theorem
experiments.objective: Verify that a resistive network and its Thevenin equivalent produce approximately the same current through a given load.
experiments.theory: Thevenin's theorem states that a linear bilateral network can be replaced at two terminals by an equivalent voltage source in series with an equivalent resistance. For this prototype, use a resistive DC network with independent sources.
procedure: With the supply off, construct the instructor-provided network and check all connections.
Disconnect the load, power the circuit within its approved limits, and measure the open-circuit terminal voltage. This is the Thevenin voltage.

Switch off and disconnect the physical supply. In the equivalent circuit calculation, replace ideal independent voltage sources with shorts and ideal independent current sources with open circuits. Never short a live supply.
Determine the equivalent resistance looking into the load terminals with the sources deactivated.
Construct the Thevenin equivalent using the calculated resistance and measured voltage; connect the same load with the supply off.
Measure the load current in each circuit and compare the results, noting resistor tolerance and measurement error.
experiments.expectedResult: The measured load current should closely match the current obtained from the Thevenin equivalent circuit, within component and measurement tolerances.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: Verification of Norton's Theorem
experiments.objective: Compare the load current of a resistive DC network with its Norton equivalent.
experiments.theory: The Norton equivalent represents a linear network by a current source in parallel with a resistance. For an independent-source resistive network, the resistance equals the Thevenin resistance.
experiments.expectedResult: Both circuits give approximately the same current through the same load.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: Maximum Power Transfer Theorem
experiments.objective: Observe how load power changes as a resistive load is varied.
experiments.theory: For a DC network with positive Thevenin resistance, maximum load power occurs when the load resistance equals the Thevenin resistance.
experiments.expectedResult: A plot of load power against load resistance peaks near the Thevenin resistance.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: RC Transient Response
experiments.objective: Observe the charging and discharging voltage of a capacitor in a series RC circuit.
experiments.theory: The time constant of a simple RC circuit is R × C. It describes how quickly the capacitor voltage approaches its final value.
experiments.expectedResult: The measured waveform follows an exponential response with a time constant close to R × C.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.
Discharge the capacitor safely using the method specified by your instructor before handling it.

experiments.title: RL Transient Response
experiments.objective: Observe the change in current after a step input to a series RL circuit.
experiments.theory: The time constant of a simple RL circuit is L / R, where R includes the resistance in the current path.
experiments.expectedResult: Current approaches its final value gradually, with a time constant close to L / R.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: RLC Circuit Response
experiments.objective: Compare the transient responses of a series RLC circuit at different resistance values.
experiments.theory: Resistance changes the damping of an RLC circuit. Depending on its component values, a step response may oscillate or approach its final value without oscillation.
experiments.expectedResult: Recorded waveforms illustrate the effect of damping on the circuit response.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: PN Junction Diode Characteristics
experiments.objective: Plot diode current against applied voltage for an instructor-approved range.
experiments.expectedResult: Forward and reverse bias produce distinctly different current–voltage characteristics.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: Zener Diode Characteristics
experiments.objective: Observe the reverse-bias voltage regulation region of a Zener diode with a current-limiting resistor.
experiments.expectedResult: The voltage varies relatively little over the permitted regulation current range.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: Half-Wave Rectifier
experiments.objective: Observe the output waveform of a diode rectifier using an isolated low-voltage AC source.
experiments.expectedResult: The load receives pulses during one half of each AC cycle.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: Full-Wave Rectifier
experiments.objective: Observe full-wave rectification using an isolated low-voltage AC source.
experiments.expectedResult: Both input half-cycles produce load current in the same direction.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

experiments.title: BJT Input and Output Characteristics
experiments.objective: Plot the input and output characteristics of an instructor-provided common-emitter BJT circuit.
experiments.expectedResult: The plots show how base current and collector-emitter voltage affect collector current.
precautions: Check component values and the instructor-approved supply limits before powering the circuit.
Avoid short circuits. Switch off the supply before modifying connections.
Use only a supervised, low-voltage teaching circuit; follow your lab manual.

branches.name: Computer Science & Engineering
branches.overview: Computer Science & Engineering explores computation, software and the systems that store, process and communicate information.

branches.name: Electronics & Communication Engineering
branches.overview: Electronics & Communication Engineering connects electronic devices, circuits and the transmission and processing of information.

branches.name: Electrical & Electronics Engineering
branches.overview: Electrical & Electronics Engineering explores electrical energy, machines, circuits and the control of physical systems.

branches.name: Mechanical Engineering
branches.overview: Mechanical Engineering studies motion, materials, energy and the design of physical machines. This short guide highlights a few connections to the current career catalogue.

branches.name: Civil Engineering
branches.overview: Civil Engineering focuses on the built environment, including structures, transportation, water and infrastructure. The links here show adjacent paths in the current catalogue, not a complete list of civil careers.

branches.name: Chemical Engineering
branches.overview: Chemical Engineering studies how materials and energy are transformed through processes. The current catalogue offers a few adjacent paths while dedicated process-engineering guides are prepared.

content_json.intro: Pivot Sols is being built for RGUKT Nuzvid students to make academic resources, practical learning and career guidance easier to find.

why.title: A place for academic resources
why.description: Useful information is often scattered across messages, folders and websites. A subject-wise collection gives students a clearer starting point.

why.title: Prepare for practical learning
why.description: Experiment guides help students understand the purpose, equipment and steps before entering the lab.

why.title: Make career options understandable
why.description: First-year students can explore what domains and roles involve, connect them to subjects and try manageable projects.

why.title: Keep the next step clear
why.description: Search, branch guides and linked resources help students move from a question to something useful.

content_json.goal: Turn common student problems into clear, useful solutions.

content_json.description: Discover academic resources, labs and career paths from one place.

cards.title: Reference Books
cards.description: Find subject-wise books and study references for your coursework.

cards.title: Lab Videos
cards.description: Watch practical demonstrations and understand experiments before entering the lab.

cards.title: Career Domains
cards.description: Explore technical fields and understand what each career path actually involves.

cards.title: Career Jobs
cards.description: Discover roles, required skills and possible career paths after graduation.
